text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German Bund futures set new highs for the day after convincingly breaking the psychologically important 100.00 mark level. Support now rests at 100.00. December Bund futures on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.22, up 0.76 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts settled almost a point higher after benign manufacturing data reassured a jittery market. But gains were capped by nerves ahead of the BoE inflation report on Wednesday and the outcome of U.S. elections. Traders said gilts were undervalued on an outright basis and on spreads. LIFFE's December long gilt future was trading at 109-13/32, up 31/32 from Monday's settlement.

FRANCE - December bond futures climbed to a contract high at 127.04, boosted by weak German data, relief at Russian President Boris Yeltsin's operation success and positive U.S. bonds. PIBOR was boosted by the French franc going back below 3.38. The December notional bond future on the MATIF settled at 126.96, up 0.62 from Monday's settlement.

ITALY - Italian bond futures jumped nearly two points to new historic highs in a general wave of buying, partly pinned to EMU hopes. Bund strength following the successful completion of Yeltsin's heart operation also helped Btps. The lira firmed slightly against the mark. December bond futures on LIFFE were trading at 125.70, up 2.00 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries extended gains to reach the day's highs. The market rose on hopes U.S. elections will produce a split government. Most expected President Bill Clinton to win reelection and the Republicans to keep a Congressional majority. Foreign buying was also seen providing the market support. Solid demand for three-year notes was expected before Tuesday's auction. December Treasury bond futures on the Chicago Board of Trade were trading at 113-30/32, up 30/32 from Monday's settlement. The long bond was quoted yielding 6.59 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese Goverment Bonds (JGB) futures contract soared to record high of 126.46, before closing at 126.40, up 0.95. In addition to buying interest from investors, the market received a boost from a media report that said the BOJ hoped the JGB market would stay bullish. In after hours trading, the December future on LIFFE was trading at 126.35, up 1.00 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - Primary market activity was capped on Tuesday by a wait-and-see mood regarding Yeltsin's heart surgery and the U.S. elections. Walt Disney stole the show with the early launch of a NZ$100 million three-year bond via Hambros Bank. Caisse Centrale Desjardins du Quebec launched a 1.0 billion French franc six-year bond to yield 28 basis points over French government paper. Kazakhstan, said to be planning a $100 million Eurobond, was awarded a BB minus long-term foreign currency rating from IBCA.
